service_categories.name: Technology
service_categories.tagline: Software, applications and platforms engineered for your business.
service_categories.short_description: Custom software, web and mobile applications, integrations, automation, design and cloud development delivered as an accountable engineering engagement.
service_categories.description:
The BUILD pillar covers everything Markedge creates: software that fits a specific process, websites and portals customers use, mobile applications for teams in the field, integrations that connect existing systems, automation that removes repetitive work, and the design and cloud foundations that make all of it usable and dependable.

Every engagement follows the same discipline: define the problem and the smallest valuable release, agree an architecture that can grow, deliver in reviewed increments with automated tests, and hand over code, environments and documentation that you own.

service_categories.name: IT Infrastructure
service_categories.tagline: IT that is maintained, monitored, secured and recoverable.
service_categories.short_description: Annual maintenance, networking, server and cloud operations, cybersecurity, backup and disaster recovery, and day-to-day IT support.
service_categories.description:
The OPERATE pillar is the work that keeps a business running: maintaining and monitoring systems, keeping networks and servers secure and patched, operating cloud environments, protecting data with tested backups, and supporting the people who use the technology every day.

Markedge defines scope, priorities and reporting in each agreement so you know exactly what is covered, what is monitored and how incidents are handled. We do not publish generic service-level promises; targets are agreed for your environment.

service_categories.name: Digital Growth
service_categories.tagline: Visibility, enquiries and conversion, measured with real data.
service_categories.short_description: Digital marketing strategy, SEO, content, social, paid media, branding, lead generation and conversion optimisation connected to first-party enquiry tracking.
service_categories.description:
The GROW pillar turns a website and digital channels into a source of enquiries. It starts with research into what customers search for and how they decide, builds content and pages that answer those questions, uses paid and social channels where they add demand, and measures everything through first-party attribution so reporting reflects business results rather than vanity metrics.

We do not promise rankings, traffic or returns. We commit to method, quality and transparent reporting.

services.name: Software Development
services.tagline: Custom software built around how your business actually works.
services.short_description: Design, engineering and delivery of business software: from requirements and architecture to release, support and continuous improvement.
services.overview:
Off-the-shelf software fits the average business. When your processes, data or customer journey are specific to you, custom software is how you stop working around tools and start working through them.

Markedge builds software as an engineering engagement, not a one-off project: we define the problem with you, agree an architecture that can grow, deliver in increments you can review, and stay responsible for what we ship.

Typical starting points are an internal process that lives in spreadsheets and email, a customer-facing portal that needs to connect to existing systems, or an ageing application that has become risky to change.

services.overview:
Businesses rarely have a data problem; they have a data movement problem. Orders live in one system, customers in another, invoices in a third, and people re-key information between them.

Markedge designs and builds the integration layer: APIs that expose your data safely, connectors that synchronise systems, and middleware that handles retries, mapping and monitoring so integrations keep working when something on either side changes.

services.short_description: Workflow automation, document processing and assisted decision-making designed around measurable business tasks rather than technology for its own sake.
services.overview:
Automation pays off when a task is frequent, well understood and expensive in people time. Most of that work can be automated with clear rules and integrations; some of it benefits from machine learning, such as classifying documents, extracting data from forms, or routing requests.

Markedge starts with the task, not the model. We map the process, automate the deterministic parts, and apply AI components only where they are accurate enough to trust and where a human remains in control of the outcome.

Every automation is measured against the manual baseline it replaces, and every AI-assisted step keeps a review path.

services.tagline: Reliable, secure networks for offices, branches and remote teams.
services.short_description: Design, implementation and maintenance of wired, wireless and site-to-site networks with segmentation, access control and monitoring.

product_documents.title: Getting started with the Lead Management System
product_documents.excerpt: Set up users, roles and your first form, then watch enquiries arrive.
product_documents.body:
1. Create users and roles

Add your sales and marketing users and give each a role. Roles control who can view, edit, assign and export leads.

2. Configure your pipeline

Review the default stages and adjust which moves are allowed and which closes require a reason. Set teams, priorities and, if you use one, a first-contact target.

3. Connect a form

Create a form with the fields you need and place it on your website. Every submission becomes a lead with its source, campaign and landing page recorded.

4. Work the pipeline

Use the board to see what is new, assign owners, schedule follow-ups and move leads through stages as you talk to prospects.

product_documents.title: Pipeline stages and follow-ups
product_documents.excerpt: How stages, owners, priorities and follow-up reminders work together.
product_documents.body:
Stages

Each lead sits in exactly one stage. Moving a lead records who moved it and when. Closing as Lost or Unqualified asks for a reason so you can report on it later.

Owners and priorities

Assigning an owner notifies that person and, for a new lead, moves it to Assigned. Priority (low to urgent) orders the board and can be set by automation rules.

Follow-ups

Schedule a call, e-mail, meeting or task with a due date. Owners are reminded before it is due; completing it records the outcome on the timeline.

product_documents.title: Reports, attribution and exports
product_documents.excerpt: Where the numbers come from and who can export them.
product_documents.body:
Attribution

Every lead stores its first touch (the visit that brought the person to you) and last touch (the visit before the enquiry). Reports use these to attribute leads to sources, campaigns and pages.

Rates

Funnel and win rates appear only where the denominator was measured. If a rate is blank, the underlying count was zero.

Exports

Exports require a permission and are written to the activity log with the user and the number of records.

product_documents.title: Getting started with the Recruitment Management System
product_documents.excerpt: Set up roles, stages and your first vacancy.
product_documents.body:
1. Users and roles

Add recruiters, hiring managers and interviewers. Roles decide what each person sees and can change.

2. Stages and scorecards

Review the default pipeline stages and define the scorecard criteria interviewers will use.

3. Open a vacancy

Raise a requisition with the brief and criteria, route it for approval, then assign the hiring team.

4. Add candidates

Create candidate profiles manually or from your careers page and move them through the stages as interviews happen.

product_documents.title: Interviews, scorecards and decisions
product_documents.excerpt: How interview rounds, structured feedback and panel decisions work.
product_documents.body:
Rounds

Each candidate can have several interview rounds, each with its own interviewers and mode. Interviewers are reminded before the interview and while feedback is pending.

Scorecards

Feedback is entered against the criteria defined for the vacancy, with a scale and a recommendation. Comparable scorecards make panel decisions faster.

Decisions

The hiring manager moves the candidate forward, to offer or to rejected, with a reason that appears in reports.

articles.title: What SEO actually means for a B2B company
articles.excerpt: SEO for a B2B business is less about keywords and more about being the clearest answer to the questions buyers ask before they enquire. Here is how it works in practice.
articles.body:
Why B2B search is different

B2B buyers research for weeks before they contact anyone. They search for problems before solutions, compare approaches before providers, and read several pages before filling in a form. SEO for a B2B company is the work of being present and credible at each of those moments.

The three layers

Technical foundation

Search engines have to crawl, render and understand the site: clean URLs, canonical tags, a sitemap, structured data, fast pages and a mobile layout. Without this, good content does not get indexed or ranked.

Intent-matched content

Each page should answer one clear intent. Commercial pages explain a service and how to buy it; informational pages explain a problem or a decision. Stuffing keywords into either makes them worse, not better.

Authority and links

References from relevant sites, consistent company information and real authorship tell search engines the content is trustworthy. Buying links or spinning content does the opposite.

What to expect

Technical fixes show results within weeks; content and authority build over months. No provider can promise rankings, because rankings depend on competitors and search engines. What you can demand is a method, transparent reporting and content that deserves to rank.

Where to start

Audit the technical foundation, map the questions your customers ask to pages, and fix the commercial pages first. Then build informational content around them and link the two together.

articles.title: Custom software or off-the-shelf: how to decide
articles.excerpt: A practical framework for deciding when an existing product is enough and when building custom software is the better investment.
articles.body:
The wrong question

"Should we build or buy?" is usually asked too early. The better question is: which of our processes are ordinary, and which are genuinely ours?

When off-the-shelf wins

  • The process is standard across your industry (accounting, payroll, e-mail).
  • An existing product covers most of the need without heavy customisation.
  • Speed matters more than fit and the workarounds are tolerable.

When custom software wins

  • The process is a differentiator and generic tools force you to change it.
  • Your data model does not fit any product without constant exceptions.
  • You need several systems to work together in a way no product offers.
  • The cost of workarounds, errors or lost time exceeds the cost of building.

A middle path

Often the answer is both: keep standard systems, and build the specific application or integration layer that connects them around your process.

How to evaluate honestly

Map the process, list the exceptions, price the workarounds, and pilot an existing product before committing. If you build, scope the smallest release that removes the biggest pain and insist on owning the code.

articles.title: What an IT AMC should include (and what to ask before signing)
articles.excerpt: Annual maintenance contracts vary widely. This guide explains what a good IT AMC covers and the questions to ask before you sign one.
articles.body:
What an AMC is for

An IT annual maintenance contract gives a business without a full IT team one accountable partner for keeping systems working. The value is in the definition: what is covered, what is monitored, how support works and what you receive in reports.

What it should include

  • An inventory of covered devices, servers, network equipment, services and licences.
  • Preventive maintenance: patching, updates, health checks on a schedule.
  • Monitoring of availability, capacity, backups and security events with defined escalation.
  • Support through a ticketed channel with agreed priorities and coverage hours.
  • Reporting that shows what was done and what needs attention.

Questions to ask

  1. What exactly is in and out of scope?
  2. What are the response and resolution targets, and how are they measured?
  3. Are backups tested, and how often?
  4. Who owns documentation and credentials?
  5. What happens at the end of the contract?

Warning signs

Vague scope, no inventory, no reporting, and promises of guaranteed uptime are signs the contract will disappoint. A good provider is specific about scope and honest about limits.

faqs.question: How do you decide between custom software and an existing product?
faqs.answer: We start by mapping the process and checking whether an existing product covers it without heavy customisation. Custom software is recommended only where the process is a genuine differentiator or existing tools would need constant workarounds.

faqs.question: Who owns the source code?
faqs.answer: You do. Code, repositories, environments and third-party accounts are set up in your name and handed over with documentation.

faqs.question: What happens after launch?
faqs.answer: Every engagement ends with a defined support and improvement plan. Ongoing maintenance can be handled through an IT AMC or a dedicated support arrangement.

faqs.question: Can we update the website ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pages are built from approved content blocks that editors manage in the CMS, with draft, review and publish states, so changes never require a developer.

faqs.question: Do you handle hosting and maintenance?
faqs.answer: Hosting, deployment, backups and monitoring are set up as part of the launch and can be maintained under an IT AMC or support arrangement.

faqs.question: Will the website be optimised for search?
faqs.answer: Technical SEO is built into the platform. Content and keyword strategy are covered by our SEO and content marketing services.

faqs.question: Do we need a native app or is a mobile website enough?
faqs.answer: If users mainly read and submit information, a responsive web application is usually faster to deliver and maintain. Native or cross-platform apps make sense for offline use, device hardware, notifications or frequent daily use.

faqs.question: Who publishes the app on the stores?
faqs.answer: The app is published under your developer accounts so you retain ownership; we manage the submission and review process with you.

faqs.question: How are updates handled?
faqs.answer: A release plan defines update cadence, testing and rollout; ongoing maintenance can be covered by a support arrangement.

faqs.question: Can you help validate the idea before building?
faqs.answer: Yes. Discovery and prototyping are designed to test assumptions cheaply before engineering starts.

faqs.question: Will the product be able to scale later?
faqs.answer: The MVP is built on foundations chosen for growth: tenant isolation, secure authentication, permissions and observability. Features are kept minimal; the foundation is not.

faqs.question: Do you take equity or build under contract?
faqs.answer: Engagements are contract-based. Commercial terms are agreed per project.

faqs.question: Can the application connect to our accounting or HR software?
faqs.answer: Integration is scoped per system. Where the system offers an API or export, data can be synchronised; where it does not, we design the least manual handover possible.

faqs.question: How do we migrate data from spreadsheets?
faqs.answer: Migration is a defined step: we clean and map the existing data with you, import it, and validate it before the old files are retired.

faqs.question: Who can change the workflow later?
faqs.answer: Configurable elements such as roles, approval steps and reference lists are managed by your administrators; structural changes are handled through support.

faqs.question: What if one of our systems has no API?
faqs.answer: We assess the available options such as exports, database access or file exchange and design the most reliable path, being clear about any limitations.

faqs.question: How are integration failures handled?
faqs.answer: Every integration is built with retries, dead-letter handling and alerts, plus a runbook that explains how to re-process failed records.

faqs.question: Can you build an API for our partners or customers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Public and partner APIs include authentication, rate limiting, versioning and documentation.

faqs.question: Do we need AI, or just automation?
faqs.answer: Often just automation. Rule-based workflows and integrations solve most repetitive work; AI components are added only where the task requires interpretation and accuracy can be validated.

faqs.question: How is our data protected?
faqs.answer: Data handling, storage location and access are agreed at the start, and AI components are chosen and configured to respect those constraints.

faqs.question: What if the automation makes a mistake?
faqs.answer: Automations log every action, route exceptions to people and keep a review path for decisions with business impact.

faqs.question: Do you design for existing products as well as new ones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Redesigns start with an audit of the current interface and usage patterns so improvements target real problems.

faqs.question: How do you validate a design?
faqs.answer: Prototypes are tested with representative users on real tasks before development begins.

faqs.question: Do you deliver a design system?
faqs.answer: For products that will keep growing, yes: tokens, components and usage guidelines shared with engineering.

faqs.question: Which cloud provider do you recommend?
faqs.answer: The recommendation depends on your existing tools, data residency needs, team skills and cost model; we assess before recommending rather than defaulting to one provider.

faqs.question: Will migration cause downtime?
faqs.answer: Migration plans define the acceptable downtime window and include rehearsal and rollback steps; many migrations can be staged to minimise interruption.

faqs.question: Who manages the cloud after migration?
faqs.answer: Either your team, with documentation and training, or Markedge through the Cloud Infrastructure service under Operate.

faqs.question: What does an IT AMC cover?
faqs.answer: Coverage is defined per contract and typically includes workstations, servers, network equipment, backups and core business applications, with preventive maintenance, monitoring and support.

faqs.question: What are the response times?
faqs.answer: Priorities and response targets are agreed in the contract based on your environment and working hours; we do not publish generic figures.

faqs.question: Does the AMC include hardware replacement?
faqs.answer: Hardware procurement and replacement are handled as separate items unless included in scope; the AMC covers diagnosis, coordination and installation.

faqs.question: Can you improve an existing network without replacing it?
faqs.answer: Often yes. A survey identifies whether the issue is coverage, capacity, configuration or equipment, and the remediation is scoped accordingly.

faqs.question: How do you secure guest and device access?
faqs.answer: Separate network segments with access control and firewall rules keep guests and IoT devices away from business systems.

faqs.question: Do you supply the equipment?
faqs.answer: Equipment can be specified and procured through us or purchased directly by you to our specification.

faqs.question: Do you manage cloud servers as well as on-premises?
faqs.answer: Yes. Physical, virtual and cloud-hosted servers are managed with the same standards, alongside the Cloud Infrastructure service for platform-level operations.

faqs.question: How are updates applied without disrupting work?
faqs.answer: Updates are scheduled in agreed windows, tested where possible, and applied with rollback plans.

faqs.question: What if we already have an IT person?
faqs.answer: Infrastructure management can complement an internal team by covering specialist tasks, out-of-hours work or documentation and standards.

faqs.question: Do we keep ownership of our cloud accounts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Accounts remain in your name; Markedge operates with scoped, auditable access that can be revoked at any time.

faqs.question: Can you reduce our cloud bill?
faqs.answer: A cost review identifies unused resources, over-sized services and missing commitments; savings depend on the environment, so we report findings rather than promise a figure.

faqs.question: What happens when something breaks at night?
faqs.answer: Alerting and the incident process are defined in the service agreement, including coverage hours and escalation.

faqs.question: Do you provide compliance certification?
faqs.answer: We help implement and evidence controls; formal certification is issued by accredited auditors, and we can prepare you for that process where relevant.

faqs.question: Where should a small business start?
faqs.answer: Multi-factor authentication, patching, tested backups, endpoint protection and access control remove the most common causes of incidents.

faqs.question: What if we have an incident now?
faqs.answer: Contact us; incident support is scoped case by case and starts with containment, evidence preservation and recovery.

faqs.question: How often should we back up?
faqs.answer: Frequency follows how much data you can afford to lose per system; critical databases may need continuous protection while file shares may be daily. The assessment sets this per system.

faqs.question: Are cloud services like e-mail backed up automatically?
faqs.answer: Providers protect their platform, not necessarily your data against deletion or ransomware; separate backups of cloud services are usually recommended.

faqs.question: How do we know the backups work?
faqs.answer: Jobs are monitored and restores are rehearsed on a schedule, with results recorded.

faqs.question: Is support remote or on site?
faqs.answer: Most issues are resolved remotely; on-site visits are included or scheduled according to the agreement.

faqs.question: Can support be combined with an AMC?
faqs.answer: Yes. IT support is commonly delivered as part of an IT AMC that also covers maintenance and monitoring.

faqs.question: How are new staff set up?
faqs.answer: Onboarding covers accounts, devices, access and security settings from a standard checklist; offboarding reverses it and documents returned assets.

faqs.question: Which channels should we use?
faqs.answer: That depends on where your customers research and decide. The research phase identifies the channels with real demand before budget is committed.

faqs.question: How do you report results?
faqs.answer: Reporting is based on first-party data: impressions, clicks, enquiries and their attribution to campaigns and pages. We do not report vanity metrics as outcomes.

faqs.question: How long before we see results?
faqs.answer: Paid channels produce data quickly; organic search and content build over months. Timelines are set per plan rather than promised generically.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee first-page rankings?
faqs.answer: No, and no honest provider can. Rankings depend on competition and search engine behaviour; we commit to method, quality and transparent reporting.

faqs.question: How is SEO different from paid search?
faqs.answer: Paid search buys placement for as long as you pay; SEO builds visibility that persists but takes longer to establish. Many businesses use both.

faqs.question: Do you write the content?
faqs.answer: We produce briefs and can write content through our content marketing service, always with your review for accuracy.

faqs.question: Which platforms matter for a B2B business?
faqs.answer: Typically professional networks and the platforms where your industry discusses its problems; the strategy phase confirms this from audience research rather than assumption.

faqs.question: Do you run paid social campaigns?
faqs.answer: Paid social is delivered through our performance marketing service and planned alongside organic content.

faqs.question: Who approves content?
faqs.answer: You do. Content is planned and reviewed in a calendar before publication.

faqs.question: What budget do we need?
faqs.answer: Budget depends on your market and objectives; planning includes a test budget to establish real costs before scaling.

faqs.question: Do we own the ad accounts?

faqs.answer: By enquiries and their quality, attributed to campaigns through first-party tracking, with cost per enquiry reported monthly.

faqs.answer: As much as can be produced well and sustained. The calendar is sized to your team's review capacity, and quality is prioritised over volume.

faqs.question: Do you use AI to generate content?

faqs.question: Do we need a rebrand or a refresh?

faqs.question: Will the new identity work on our website?

faqs.question: How many leads will we get?
